context: Reference coverage: a skill written from a one-round conversation about pull request descriptions, not code. A good answer writes a SKILL.md whose description names the task and the words a user would type, a hard stop that comes from the correction and nothing invented beyond it, a numbered workflow ending in a check, a references file with the not-like-this and like-this pair and the why, and one eval whose task is a different change than the conversation's, carries no hint of the answer, and weights the habit.

checklist.name: Writes the four files with valid front matter
checklist.description: Creates skills/<name>/SKILL.md with front matter holding a kebab-case name and a description, skills/<name>/references/examples.md, and one evals-reference/01-<slug>/ folder holding task.md and a criteria.json that parses as a weighted checklist.

checklist.name: Description names the task and the trigger words
checklist.description: The description says in the third person what the skill does (writing the description of a pull request or merge request) and lists situations in the words a user would type, such as open a PR, write the PR body, describe this change, ending with a phrase like even if the user never asks for a structure, and says what it is not for.

checklist.name: Hard stop traces to the correction
checklist.description: SKILL.md has one or two hard stops, and each is the correction the user made (never a list of changed files; lead with why, then the change in behavior, then how it was verified). No rule is added that the conversation does not support, such as rules about titles, labels, reviewers, emoji, or length.

checklist.name: Workflow ends in a check
checklist.description: SKILL.md has a numbered workflow whose last step is something the agent can tell is done, such as the description has the three parts in order and names no file list.

checklist.name: References carry the pair and the why
checklist.description: references/examples.md shows the file list under a not-like-this heading and the why-what-verified version under a like-this heading, in the conversation's own domain, with a one-sentence why taken from the correction.

checklist.name: Eval task is realistic, in another domain, and gives nothing away
checklist.description: The eval task.md is a prompt someone would type (a branch or diff summary and a request for the pull request description), is about a different change than a rate limiter, and does not say to lead with why, to describe behavior, to mention verification, or to avoid a file list.

checklist.name: Eval checklist weights the habit
checklist.description: criteria.json gives most of its points to the habit (why first, behavior change next, verification last, no file list) and a minority to accuracy against the given change and scope.

checklist.name: Nothing speculative or copied
checklist.description: The skill text does not quote the eval's change or identifiers, does not mention scores or scenarios, and does not promise behaviors the conversation never showed.
